experiment: Prospective-in-execution prediction vs public historical coin catalogue; NOT prospective semantic gold
search_to_begin_after_commit: Find the first other museum-inventoried physical coin described as Arse-Saguntum, 130-72 BCE, bronze one-and-a-half unit, obverse helmeted Roma head and reverse prow + Victory + caduceus; exclude MARQ NIM 727 and any mere listing of its photograph.
no_cherry_pick: Record the first qualifying object and its catalogue legend, even if false; record every inspected failed candidate and why it did not qualify.
rule: If the new physical coin matches the full object type, predict a Latin SAGVNT-family label on the obverse and Iberian ARSE on the reverse, with reverse ARSE serving as issuer/ethnic-toponym in the known Arse-Saguntum series.
alternatives: H1 bilingual Latin SAGVNT-family on obverse AND Iberian ARSE on reverse
H2 only Latin city label, no ARSE
H3 only Iberian ARSE, no Latin city label
success_for_one_coin: Both reading families confirmed from catalogued photographs of the first eligible different physical specimen. This is a technical retrospective cross-item replication, NOT a new decipherment.
failure: Any eligible coin without both; disagreement about specimen classification or unreadable photographs requires abstention, no automatic success.
inherited_exposure: The coin series function and reading variants were already publicly documented, so cannot establish linguistic novelty or independent blind contextual gold even if successful.
scoring: Report count of qualifying physical coins, family/dependency grouping, success/failure/abstention. Do not compute a statistically meaningful accuracy from one specimen.
dates_and_lock: GitHub immutable commit SHA/time externally verifiable; authoring date not itself timestamp proof.
